kjv: instruments of cruelty are in their (Simeon and Levi's) habitations
mine: their (Simeon and Levi's) blades are weapons of violence
note: mekheroteihem is a hapax, probably "swords/blades" (cf. Greek machaira); the KJV guesses "habitations" from a root meaning "dwell". Context: swords (medium confidence). Mekheroteihem is a hapax. 'Swords/blades' (perhaps related to Greek machaira, as Rashi already noted) fits the recollection of Gen 34:25, where Simeon and Levi 'took their swords', and is the reading of ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV, CSB and NET. The derivation remains uncertain. Other possible meanings: (1) 'their habitations / land of sojourning' (from gur) — Targum Onkelos, KJV; (2) 'their origin/kinship' (cf. mekhorah, Ezek 16:3) — some medieval and modern interpreters; (3) 'their schemes' (from karah 'plot') — LXX ex haireseos auton ('of their own choice'), some commentators; (4) 'their weapons' generally — NJPS.

kjv: they (Simeon and Levi) digged down a wall
note: 'iqqeru-shor: 'iqqer means to hamstring and shor is "ox"; the KJV read shur "wall" and gave the verb a sense of digging.

kjv: O my (Jacob's) soul, come not thou into their (Simeon and Levi's) secret
mine: Let me (Jacob) not enter their (Simeon and Levi's) council
note: nafshi is idiomatic for "I/myself" and sod means council; the KJV renders both woodenly.
lavi' most likely means lion or lioness, not specifically an old lion.

kjv: until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be
mine: until he comes to whom it belongs, and the obedience of the peoples is his
note: shiloh is one of the most debated cruxes: it may be a name, "Shiloh" the town, or shello "(he) to whom it belongs" (cf. Ezek 21:32). yiqqehat means "obedience", not "gathering". Both readings are read messianically. Context: until he comes to whom it belongs (medium confidence). Reading shello 'whose it is' has the widest ancient support: Ezek 21:32 (Eng 21:27) 'until he comes whose right it is', LXX (ta apokeimena auto / ho apokeitai), Symmachus, Peshitta and the Targums ('until Messiah comes, whose is the kingdom'). The parallel 'the obedience of the peoples is his' needs a person. NIV and NET agree. Other possible meanings: (1) 'until Shiloh comes', a personal (messianic) name — KJV, NASB, Talmud (Sanh 98b), Genesis Rabbah; (2) 'until tribute comes to him' (shay lo) — ESV, NRSV, NJPS; (3) 'until he comes to Shiloh' (the town) — some medieval and critical scholars; (4) 'until his ruler comes' (Akkadian shelu) — a few modern scholars. Also 'gathering' (KJV) for yiqqehat 'obedience'.

kjv: a lawgiver from between his (Judah's) feet
mine: the ruler's staff from between his (Judah's) feet
note: mechoqeq can mean "commander" or "commander's staff"; the parallel with "scepter" favours the staff.

kjv: His (Judah's) eyes shall be red with wine
mine: His (Judah's) eyes are darker than wine
note: chakhlili is rare ("dull/dark" or "sparkling"); the min can be comparative ("than wine") or causal ("from wine").
mishpetayim (dual) most likely means sheepfolds or saddlebags; "two burdens" is a guess.

kjv: a troop shall overcome him (Gad): but he shall overcome at the last
mine: raiders shall raid him (Gad), but he shall raid at their heels
note: The verse puns on gad/gedud/yagud; 'aqev means "heel", not "at the last".

kjv: whose branches run over the wall
mine: its shoots climb over the wall
note: banot tsa'adah, literally "daughters (that) step", is obscure. Some read it as wild asses ("Joseph is a wild colt"), not a vine.

kjv: Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf
note: Ravin (to devour, plunder) is obsolete; the Hebrew ze'ev yitraf means "a wolf that tears".
